<br>
<br>

<p>
To create a web app for this new version of the Classless CP system, we'll need a front-end to allow users to select their features, classes, and multiclass options, while also tracking their CP progression. We’ll also need a backend (if desired for persistence) or local storage to hold the data. Here's an outline of the web app structure, followed by code examples for each part.<br>
Key Features of the App:
</p>

<p>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
Class and Feature Selection: Users can select classes, pick features, and assign CP to them.
</div>
</p>

<p>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
Progress Tracking: The app tracks the CP spent and adjusts the available features for each level.
</div>
</p>

<p>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
Multiclassing: Users can combine multiple classes and balance features accordingly.
</div>
</p>

<p>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
Spellcasting: Spellcasting classes will have their spell slots and progression tracked.
</div>
</p>

<p>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
Dynamic CP Management: The app will ensure that users can’t select features too early or purchase features ahead of when they're unlocked.
</div>
</p>

<p>
Tech Stack
</p>

<p>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
Frontend: React.js (for dynamic and interactive UI)
</div>
</p>

<p>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
Backend: Could be optional. For simplicity, we’ll use local storage to store data (or a simple Node.js/Express backend if persistence is required).
</div>
</p>

<p>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
State Management: React’s useState and useEffect to track CP, features, and progression.
</div>
</p>

<p>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
Styling: CSS-in-JS (using libraries like styled-components or Emotion) for easy, maintainable styles.
</div>
</p>

<p>
<ol type="1" start="1">
<li>Setting Up the Frontend (React App)</li>
</ol>
</p>

<p>
First, let's set up a basic React app structure.
</p>

<p>
npx create-react-app classless-cp-builder<br>
cd classless-cp-builder<br>
npm start
</p>

<p>
<ol type="1" start="2">
<li>Components Breakdown</li>
</ol>
</p>

<p>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
App.js: Main component where classes and features are initialized and CP is tracked.
</div>
</p>

<p>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
FeatureSelector.js: Component for selecting features.
</div>
</p>

<p>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
ClassSelector.js: Component to select classes and manage CP.
</div>
</p>

<p>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
ProgressionTracker.js: Shows CP usage and progression (how much CP has been spent, remaining CP, etc.).
</div>
</p>

<p>
<ol type="1" start="3">
<li>Implementing Components</li>
</ol>
App.js
</p>

<p>
This is the main entry point where we will bring everything together.
</p>

<p>
import React, { useState, useEffect } from "react";<br>
import ClassSelector from "./ClassSelector";<br>
import FeatureSelector from "./FeatureSelector";<br>
import ProgressionTracker from "./ProgressionTracker";
</p>

<p>
const App = () =&gt; {<br>
  const [cp, setCp] = useState(3); // Start with 3 CP at level 1<br>
  const [selectedClass, setSelectedClass] = useState("");<br>
  const [selectedFeatures, setSelectedFeatures] = useState([]);<br>
  const [availableFeatures, setAvailableFeatures] = useState([]);<br>
  const [level, setLevel] = useState(1);
</p>

<p>
  // Class data: Level-up progression for CP and available features<br>
  const classes = [<br>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
{<br>
  name: "Barbarian",<br>
  features: [
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 60pt'>
{ name: "Rage", cpCost: 3, requiredLevel: 1 },<br>
{ name: "Reckless Attack", cpCost: 3, requiredLevel: 2 },<br>
{ name: "Extra Attack", cpCost: 3, requiredLevel: 5 },<br>
// More features...
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
  ],<br>
},<br>
{<br>
  name: "Fighter",<br>
  features: [
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 60pt'>
{ name: "Fighting Style", cpCost: 2, requiredLevel: 1 },<br>
{ name: "Action Surge", cpCost: 3, requiredLevel: 2 },<br>
{ name: "Extra Attack", cpCost: 3, requiredLevel: 5 },<br>
// More features...
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
  ],<br>
},<br>
// Add other classes here...
</div>
  ];
</p>

<p>
  // Update available features when a class is selected<br>
  useEffect(() =&gt; {<br>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
if (selectedClass) {<br>
  const classData = classes.find((cls) =&gt; cls.name === selectedClass);<br>
  setAvailableFeatures(classData.features.filter(f =&gt; f.requiredLevel &lt;= level));<br>
}
</div>
  }, [selectedClass, level]);
</p>

<p>
  // Handle adding a feature<br>
  const handleAddFeature = (feature) =&gt; {<br>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
if (cp &gt;= feature.cpCost) {<br>
  setSelectedFeatures([...selectedFeatures, feature]);<br>
  setCp(cp - feature.cpCost); // Deduct CP cost<br>
} else {<br>
  alert("Not enough CP to add this feature!");<br>
}
</div>
  };
</p>

<p>
  return (<br>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
&lt;div&gt;<br>
  &lt;h1&gt;Classless CP Character Builder&lt;/h1&gt;
</div>
</p>

<p>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
  &lt;ClassSelector classes={classes} setSelectedClass={setSelectedClass} setLevel={setLevel} /&gt;<br>
  &lt;ProgressionTracker cp={cp} level={level} selectedFeatures={selectedFeatures} /&gt;
</div>
</p>

<p>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
  {selectedClass &amp;&amp; (
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 60pt'>
&lt;FeatureSelector<br>
  availableFeatures={availableFeatures}<br>
  handleAddFeature={handleAddFeature}<br>
/&gt;
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
  )}<br>
&lt;/div&gt;
</div>
  );<br>
};
</p>

<p>
export default App;
</p>

<p>
ClassSelector.js
</p>

<p>
This component allows users to select a class.
</p>

<p>
import React from "react";
</p>

<p>
const ClassSelector = ({ classes, setSelectedClass, setLevel }) =&gt; {<br>
  const handleClassChange = (event) =&gt; {<br>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
setSelectedClass(event.target.value);<br>
setLevel(1); // Reset to level 1 when a new class is selected
</div>
  };
</p>

<p>
  return (<br>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
&lt;div&gt;<br>
  &lt;h3&gt;Select Class&lt;/h3&gt;<br>
  &lt;select onChange={handleClassChange}&gt;
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 60pt'>
&lt;option value=""&gt;Select a Class&lt;/option&gt;<br>
{classes.map((cls, idx) =&gt; (<br>
  &lt;option value={cls.name} key={idx}&gt;
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 90pt'>
{cls.name}
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 60pt'>
  &lt;/option&gt;<br>
))}
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
  &lt;/select&gt;<br>
&lt;/div&gt;
</div>
  );<br>
};
</p>

<p>
export default ClassSelector;
</p>

<p>
FeatureSelector.js
</p>

<p>
This component allows users to choose features to purchase with their CP.
</p>

<p>
import React from "react";
</p>

<p>
const FeatureSelector = ({ availableFeatures, handleAddFeature }) =&gt; {<br>
  return (<br>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
&lt;div&gt;<br>
  &lt;h3&gt;Select Features&lt;/h3&gt;<br>
  &lt;ul&gt;
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 60pt'>
{availableFeatures.map((feature, index) =&gt; (<br>
  &lt;li key={index}&gt;
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 90pt'>
&lt;button onClick={() =&gt; handleAddFeature(feature)}&gt;<br>
  {feature.name} (CP: {feature.cpCost})<br>
&lt;/button&gt;
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 60pt'>
  &lt;/li&gt;<br>
))}
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
  &lt;/ul&gt;<br>
&lt;/div&gt;
</div>
  );<br>
};
</p>

<p>
export default FeatureSelector;
</p>

<p>
ProgressionTracker.js
</p>

<p>
This component displays the current CP and progression information.
</p>

<p>
import React from "react";
</p>

<p>
const ProgressionTracker = ({ cp, level, selectedFeatures }) =&gt; {<br>
  return (<br>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
&lt;div&gt;<br>
  &lt;h3&gt;Progression Tracker&lt;/h3&gt;<br>
  &lt;p&gt;Level: {level}&lt;/p&gt;<br>
  &lt;p&gt;Available CP: {cp}&lt;/p&gt;<br>
  &lt;h4&gt;Selected Features&lt;/h4&gt;<br>
  &lt;ul&gt;
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 60pt'>
{selectedFeatures.map((feature, index) =&gt; (<br>
  &lt;li key={index}&gt;{feature.name}&lt;/li&gt;<br>
))}
</div>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
  &lt;/ul&gt;<br>
&lt;/div&gt;
</div>
  );<br>
};
</p>

<p>
export default ProgressionTracker;
</p>

<p>
<ol type="1" start="4">
<li>Enhancements</li>
</ol>
Persistent Data:
</p>

<p>
To persist character data across page reloads, you can use local storage. Here's how to implement it:
</p>

<p>
useEffect(() =&gt; {<br>
  const storedData = localStorage.getItem("characterData");<br>
  if (storedData) {<br>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
const data = JSON.parse(storedData);<br>
setCp(data.cp);<br>
setLevel(data.level);<br>
setSelectedClass(data.selectedClass);<br>
setSelectedFeatures(data.selectedFeatures);
</div>
  }<br>
}, []);
</p>

<p>
useEffect(() =&gt; {<br>
  const characterData = {<br>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
cp,<br>
level,<br>
selectedClass,<br>
selectedFeatures,
</div>
  };<br>
  localStorage.setItem("characterData", JSON.stringify(characterData));<br>
}, [cp, level, selectedClass, selectedFeatures]);
</p>

<p>
This will save and load the character data from local storage automatically when the app is loaded.<br>
<ol type="1" start="5">
<li>Running the App</li>
</ol>
</p>

<p>
Now, with everything set up, run the app:
</p>

<p>
npm start
</p>

<p>
The application will launch, and you'll have a web-based character builder for the Classless CP system where you can:
</p>

<p>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
Select a class,
</div>
</p>

<p>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
Choose and purchase features with CP,
</div>
</p>

<p>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
Track your progression through levels,
</div>
</p>

<p>
<div style='padding-left: 30pt'>
Ensure CP is spent appropriately.
</div>
</p>

<p>
<ol type="1" start="6">

</p>

</div>
</p>

<p>

<p>
